scope: Integration of the requested Javier Parcet, Sarah Peluse and Jesse Peterson reports. Peluse reuses the existing number-theory overview and reference, with an additional Analysis entry. The nine registered reports are a selected and cross-listed collection, not a complete Analysis-section roster.

mathematicalReview.scope: The coordinator read all 105 new atomic notes, the three overviews and report records. Parcet and Peterson were checked against their formal report bodies; Peluse was checked against selected passages and the previously imported notes. The Peluse worker independently reviewed the early Parcet foundations. These reviews do not constitute independent verification of every cited research proof.
mathematicalReview.sourceScope: Formal Proceedings sources are recorded in the reference pages. Peluse is in Volume 3 and is cross-listed here. Selected Das-Peterson 2022 passages support the hyperstate and Poisson-boundary definitions; no full reading of that supplementary article is claimed.
corrections: Reused the existing Peluse overview 0GO0 and reference rather than creating a duplicate overview at 0Y00. Number-theory narrative ownership and existing topic links were retained.
Separated finite-cyclic Fourier normalization from the integer and Euclidean conventions. Checked conjugations, powers in Gowers identities and the signs in the one- and two-frequency expansions.
Kept the two-frequency polynomial identity separate from the estimates needed for quantitative density bounds. Retained degree-versus-coefficient dependence in Peluse's local inverse theorem.
Defined normality for arbitrary Schur maps by ultraweak continuity. Retained the second-variable-linear inner-product convention in kernels, Gram symbols and group traces.

Separated discrete group traces from the locally compact Plancherel-trace construction. Retained the positive-dimension hypothesis in local Lie-group estimates and strict high-rank exponent thresholds.

Kept C0 in the SL3 decay statement, and kept critical-exponent claims as conjectures. Deferred the global HM branch where the source's zeroth-order decay prose needs reconciliation with the constant symbol.
Restricted the no-expectation proper-proximality definition to finite factors, and did not treat the relative closure of compact operators as a C*-algebra.
Retained normal, regular, symmetric and generating hyperstate assumptions where needed. Specified the right-random-walk convention and the regular crossed-product representation.
Added explicit body links for the new foundational dependencies and reconciled the prerequisite records after the shared operator-algebra pages were written.
